[assistant] Save this file as: ``` docs/NEURALTUBE_WORKER_FABRIC.md ``` This document tells **Gemini / Codex / AI coding agents exactly how NeuralTube processes signals in parallel**, which is essential for performance and stability. --- # NeuralTube Worker Fabric ## Purpose The Worker Fabric defines the **parallel processing architecture** used by NeuralTube. Instead of running all analysis on the main thread, tasks are distributed across multiple workers. This allows the system to process: ``` thousands of signals multiple narratives real-time intelligence updates ``` without blocking the interface or slowing down the pipeline. --- # Worker Fabric Overview The Worker Fabric acts as a **task distribution layer** between engines. ``` Signal Pipeline ↓ Worker Fabric ↓ Parallel Processing ↓ Results Returned to Engines ``` The Worker Fabric manages: ``` task queues worker threads task scheduling result aggregation ``` --- # Worker Types NeuralTube workers should be specialized for different tasks. Recommended worker types: ``` ingestion workers normalization workers clustering workers intelligence workers research workers ``` Each worker type processes a different stage of the pipeline. --- # Worker Roles ### Ingestion Workers Responsible for collecting signals from platforms. Tasks: ``` fetch new videos retrieve metadata queue signals for normalization ``` --- ### Normalization Workers Responsible for standardizing signals. Tasks: ``` normalize metadata extract content prepare signals for clustering ``` --- ### Clustering Workers Responsible for narrative detection. Tasks: ``` group signals into narratives update narrative velocity track signal counts ``` --- ### Intelligence Workers Responsible for higher-level analysis. Tasks: ``` build influence graphs run contradiction analysis generate forecasts detect anomalies ``` --- ### Research Workers Responsible for autonomous investigation. Tasks: ``` search additional platforms collect missing signals expand narrative datasets ``` --- # Worker Pool Workers should run in a pool. Example configuration: ``` Ingestion Workers: 2 Normalization Workers: 2 Clustering Workers: 2 Intelligence Workers: 2 Research Workers: 1 ``` Total workers: ``` 9 ``` This configuration can scale based on system load. --- # Worker Manager The Worker Fabric must be controlled by a central manager. File location: ``` src/system/workerFabricEngine.js ``` Responsibilities: ``` create worker pools assign tasks monitor worker health restart failed workers balance workloads ``` Example interface: ``` startWorkerPool() dispatchTask(task) getWorkerStatus() restartWorker(workerId) ``` --- # Task Queue Tasks must be placed into a central queue before execution. Example queue structure: ``` task_id task_type payload priority created_at ``` Example task: ``` task_id: TASK_001 task_type: clustering payload: signal_batch priority: medium ``` Tasks are consumed by workers matching the task type. --- # Worker Communication Workers communicate through the **Signal Bus**. Example flow: ``` SignalIngestionEngine ↓ Worker Fabric ↓ Normalization Worker ↓ Signal Bus ↓ NarrativeClusterEngine ``` This allows engines and workers to remain loosely coupled. --- # Worker Execution Example Example worker loop: ```javascript while (workerActive) { const task = TaskQueue.getNext() if (task.type === "normalization") { normalizeSignal(task.payload) } if (task.type === "clustering") { clusterSignals(task.payload) } if (task.type === "intelligence") { runIntelligenceEngines(task.payload) } } ``` Workers continuously process queued tasks. --- # Fault Tolerance The Worker Fabric must detect worker failures. If a worker crashes: ``` detect failure log event restart worker requeue unfinished task ``` Example log entry: ``` Worker 3 crashed Restarting worker Requeued task TASK_104 ``` --- # Worker Scaling Worker count should scale based on system load. Example scaling rules: ``` signal rate < 50/min → 4 workers signal rate < 200/min → 8 workers signal rate > 200/min → 16 workers ``` The Worker Fabric should adjust worker counts automatically if possible. --- # Monitoring Worker health must be visible in Mission Control. Example status: ``` Workers Active: 9 Workers Healthy: 9 Queued Tasks: 14 Processing Rate: 220 tasks/min ``` --- # Performance Goals The Worker Fabric should support: ``` thousands of signals per hour low latency processing parallel engine execution system stability under load ``` Target latency: ``` signal ingestion → narrative detection < 30 seconds ``` --- # Worker Directory Structure Recommended structure: ``` src/workers/ingestion/ src/workers/normalization/ src/workers/clustering/ src/workers/intelligence/ src/workers/research/ ``` Each worker type should have its own implementation file. --- # End State When the Worker Fabric is fully implemented NeuralTube becomes capable of: ``` real-time signal ingestion large-scale narrative analysis parallel intelligence processing stable autonomous investigations ``` The Worker Fabric enables the platform to scale from a prototype to a **production intelligence system**. --- ## Next Document for Gemini The next file that will dramatically improve the build is: ``` docs/NEURALTUBE_UI_ARCHITECTURE.md ``` This defines: ``` dashboard layout operator panels investigation workspace mission control command interface ``` Without it, coding agents will create **inconsistent UI components** and the interface will become chaotic.
